title: Application for Regular Bail under Section 480 read with Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
whenToUse: Use when an accused has been arrested and remanded to judicial custody, seeking regular bail under Section 480 or Section 483 BNSS, 2023 before Magistrate, Sessions or High Court.
variantComparisonNote: Post-arrest regular bail petition. Distinct from pre-arrest anticipatory bail under Section 482 BNSS and default bail under Section 187 BNSS.
youWillNeed: Copy of FIR, remand orders, arrest memo, proof of medical ailments/age, local solvent surety documents.
legalBasis: Sections 480, 483 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS); P. Chidambaram v. CBI (2019); Sanjay Chandra v. CBI (2012).
mandatoryStatutoryIngredients: Accused is in actual custody and remanded under Section 187 BNSS
Investigation substantially completed or custodial interrogation no longer warranted
Principle of 'Bail is the rule, jail is the exception' established
No risk of flight, witness intimidation, or evidence tampering

particulars.label: Accused / Applicant Name
particulars.description: Full name of undertrial in custody

particulars.label: Date of Arrest
particulars.description: Date when accused was taken into custody

aiBlocks.title: Custodial History & Nature of Allegations
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Narrate date of arrest, duration of incarceration since {{FACT:arrest_date}}, completion of police remand, and absence of necessity for further detention.

aiBlocks.title: Grounds for Enlargement on Regular Bail
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Establish lack of prima facie case, parity with co-accused, roots in society, no flight risk, and trial unlikely to conclude expeditiously.

aiBlocks.title: Undertaking & Final Bail Prayer
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Offer solvent local sureties, undertaking to surrender passport, attend trial hearings, and pray for release on regular bail.
